q: What carbon figure should a buyer of Jubail polyethylene ask for?
title: Jubail polyethylene: buyer carbon figure
short: Polyethylene is not a CBAM good, so the request is for Scope 3. Ask for a cradle to gate figure per tonne of resin that covers ethane or naphtha cracking, polymerisation, steam and electricity, with the method and year. Do not use a generic European average for Saudi resin.
audience: Packaging, film and moulding companies buying polyethylene from Jubail producers

ul: Feedstock extraction and processing up to the cracker.
Cracking furnaces, which are the largest direct source.
Polymerisation, steam, electricity and site utilities.
Whether biogenic or recycled content claims are by mass balance, and how that is allocated.
The allocation between ethylene and co-products from the cracker.
The year and method, such as ISO 14067.

p: Use a published regional figure for the resin type and label it as an estimate in your Scope 3 total.

senseible: Senseible reads supplier invoices into a dated, fingerprinted record and keeps each supplier's own figure beside the purchase it belongs to, so a Scope 3 total shows which numbers are primary data and which are estimates.
